story: A Google AI answer gave a Kodiak hunter the wrong snipe opening day, she shot three snipe, turned herself in, and was fined $150. The one source of truth is the state regulation, which the state itself calls simplified.
fact_check: two adversarial validators, 2026-09-30. SINGLE-SOURCE STORY: c1-c12 rest on one Alaska Beacon report (via KTOO) built on a trooper affidavit and on-record DPS quotes. c13-c15 are primary (ADF&G, Google). Anything not in this file may not appear on screen or in the VO.
cultural_rules: No Alaska Native subjects or sources in this story. Do not imply any.
banned_from_screen: Wilson's snipe as a fact about the birds shot (photo caption only)
any snipe date other than Oct 8 attributed to the affidavit
ignorance of the law is no excuse

claims.spoken: A Kodiak woman searched Google for snipe season on her phone.
claims.verbatim_source: "Christina stated that she Googled 'Snipe season' on her phone and that, according to Google, snipe season began on September 1st."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th, quoting Trooper Alex Wick's affidavit

claims.spoken: The answer said the season had already begun, on September first.
claims.verbatim_source: "according to Google, snipe season began on September 1st."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th, quoting the trooper's affidavit
requires: attribute to the trooper's affidavit as the Beacon relays it; never state the Sept 1 claim as ADF&G's or Google's published text

claims.spoken: On September fifth she shot three snipe.
claims.verbatim_source: "Incorrect information provided by a Google AI overview caused a Kodiak woman to hunt snipe illegally on Sept. 5" / "she hunted three snipe"
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th

claims.spoken: Under the general season, snipe weren't legal to take until October eighth.
claims.verbatim_source: "After conducting her own research, she learned that snipes are not legal to take under the general season until October 8th."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th, quoting the affidavit
requires: Oct 8 is sourced ONLY to the Beacon quoting the affidavit; ADF&G booklet did not load. Never call it Kodiak zone. Never say Google invented a date.

claims.spoken: She called troopers and turned herself in.
claims.verbatim_source: "Christina then contacted dispatch to turn herself in." / "Alaska Wildlife Trooper Alex Wick said Christina Weaver called troopers to self-report the violation."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th

claims.spoken: The trooper ran the same search and got the same wrong answer.
claims.verbatim_source: "He said he performed a Google search identical to Weaver's and received identical incorrect information."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th, the trooper's affidavit as relayed

claims.spoken: She pleaded no contest and was fined a hundred and fifty dollars.
claims.verbatim_source: "Weaver pleaded no contest to the citation on Friday and was fined $150."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th
requires: state $150 only; no other penalty; no plea date

claims.spoken: Her own words were, I feel terrible.
claims.verbatim_source: "I feel terrible, and I have a lot of shame with it. Obviously, that's why I immediately self-reported once I got home and dived into the regs."
claims.source_label: Christina Weaver, phone interview, Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th
requires: exact words only; attribute to Weaver

claims.spoken: A state spokesman said this may be the first time he has seen AI cited.
claims.on_screen: "THE FIRST TIME I THINK WE HAVE SEEN AI CITED"
claims.verbatim_source: "This is the first time that I think we have seen AI cited."
claims.source_label: Austin McDaniel, Alaska Department of Public Safety spokesman, Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th
requires: keep the hedge I think; attribute to McDaniel

claims.spoken: He said the one source of truth is Fish and Game's regulations and emergency orders.
claims.on_screen: ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH · ADF&G REGULATIONS
claims.verbatim_source: "The one source of truth when it comes to hunts is the Alaska Department of Fish and Game's regulations and emergency orders."
claims.source_label: Austin McDaniel, DPS, Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th
requires: McDaniel's line, DPS, not an ADF&G statement

claims.spoken: He expects more of this in the future.
claims.on_screen: "I EXPECT WE'LL SEE MORE OF THIS"
claims.verbatim_source: "I expect we'll see more of this type of thing in the future."
claims.source_label: Austin McDaniel, DPS, Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th

claims.spoken: Google did not respond to a request for comment.
claims.verbatim_source: "Google did not respond to an email seeking comment on the incorrect information provided by its software."
claims.source_label: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), via KTOO, September 28th

claims.spoken: Fish and Game says its online regulations are simplified, not quoted from state law, and that emergency orders can take precedence.
claims.on_screen: REGULATIONS ARE SIMPLIFIED · EMERGENCY ORDERS CAN OVERRIDE
claims.verbatim_source: "These regulations are not quoted verbatim from state law. They have been simplified for your convenience. In addition, be aware that issued emergency orders may contain hunting and trapping season information which may take precedence over information in the Hunting and Trapping Regulation booklets found below."

claims.spoken: Fish and Game will mail you the regulations or you can call the office.
claims.verbatim_source: "You may request a hard copy of the Alaska Hunting Regulations by emailing dfg.dwc.hq-info@alaska.gov, by calling (907) 465-4190, or pick up a copy of the regulations at your nearest Fish and Game Office."

claims.spoken: Google's own help page says AI responses may include mistakes and to check important info in more than one place.
claims.verbatim_source: "AI responses may include mistakes. | ...AI Overviews can and will make mistakes. | Always check important info in more than one place."
requires: quote Google's page; do not say Google admitted this snipe answer was wrong
